summary: Takao Yamagata (1932–2019) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1951–1958). He served on the faculty at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1970–2003) and was president of the Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).

Takashi Iwata (born 1944) specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg under Akira Hirakawa, Ernst Steinkellner, Albrecht Wezler, and Lambert Schmithausen, later serving as professor at Waseda University (~1992–2014).

Takashi Koezuka (born 1939) is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. His academic career includes appointments at Osaka University, where he served as professor (attested 2001) and professor emeritus (attested 2012).

Takashi Maeda (born 1943) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University and later served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995 and 2006).

Takashi Matsuura is a linguist and Indologist who completed his B.A. (2003–2005) and Ph.D. (2020–2021) at the University of Tokyo. He has served there as assistant professor (2022) and held lecturer and instructor positions at several universities.

Takashi Nakao (1931–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Rissho University and Tokyo University of Education (doctoral degree, 1974), taught at Bunkyo University Women's College, and served at Rissho University (1979–2002; emeritus professor).

Takashi Ogawa (born 1961) works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University, Peking University, and the University of Tokyo (doctoral degree, 2009). He held positions at Komazawa University (1991) and Tokyo International University (2024).

Takashi Yamada (born 1954) is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He was educated at Hosei University and served as an associate professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto (attested 2003).
Takatoshi Ito is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Komazawa University, with his tenure attested in 1981 and 1991.

Takatoshi Nakamura is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Ryukai Mano in 1979. He served as a researcher at the Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute of Taisho University (attested 1978).

Takatsugu Hayashi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Delhi. He has held positions at Tohoku University, Sendai National College of Technology, Hosen Gakuen College, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Takayasu Higuchi (1919–2015) studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1943) and served there as professor of archaeology (~1958–1983). He later directed the Research Centre for Silk Roadology, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Sen-oku Matsurokan, and Sen-oku Hakuko Kan.

Takayasu Kimura (born 1934) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University and was attested in 1995 as a lecturer at Taisho University and researcher at the Institute of Modern Religious Education of Shingon Buzan.
Takayasu Suzuki (born 1964) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1983–1993) and served as a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University (~2011).

Takayoshi Kamei (1886–1977) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1907–1910) and held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1928–1947), Ibaraki University (~1949–1957), and Seisen University (~1957–1970).

Takayoshi Namikawa (born 1947) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his undergraduate and doctoral degrees at Bukkyo University, where he became a professor in 1981 and emeritus professor in 2018, and held visiting roles at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Takayuki Hirosawa is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He has held academic appointments at Taisho University, serving as a group member through 1991 and later as professor (attested 2014).

Takehiro Sueki (1921–2007) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1941–1944). He held academic posts at the University of Electro-Communications (~1954–1968), the University of Tokyo (~1968–1982), and Toyo University (~1982–1992).

Takeo Hibino (1914–2007) studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936), where he later worked at the Institute for Research in Humanities and as an assistant (1948–1977). He also served as professor at Otemon Gakuin University and professor and president at Otemae University.

Takeo Kanaseki (1897–1983) was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Kyoto University (~1919–1923). He held academic posts at Kyushu University (~1936–1960), Tezukayama Gakuin University (~1960–1979), and Tottori University.
